title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quality evaluation of the prompt set, discuss recent regressions on intent detection, refine scoring rubric, and agree next steps for a 10k prompt regression run and security documentation. Customer expressed concern about a fallback policy and SSO/KMS integration timeline.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-19 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Carlos (BlueWave Head of ML), Priya (PM), Liam (SRE), Dana (Data Scientist)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:05] Carlos: Carlos here
[00:07] Priya: Priya here
[00:09] Liam: Liam on
[00:10] Dana: Dana yes
[00:12] Maya: perfect, so quick agenda — quality eval updates from your side, we have the scoring spreadsheet that we sent last week, any surprises? Ethan will kick off with the numbers.

[00:29] Ethan: yeah, thanks Maya. So we ran the eval over the 1,200 prompt dev set, overall pass rate for intent detection is 87% on the current Redwood tuned model, which is down from 92% in last week's run; looks like the changes to prompt framing for the billing intents caused some drift.

[00:50] Carlos: hmm, 87%, that's a bit of a regression; do you see which cases dropped?

[01:05] Ethan: primarily the multi-step billing flows and some edge entity extraction when the customer mixes free-text and form fields. Also, the KV cache warm-start seems to be dropping tokens for long contexts — maybe KV cash, sorry, cache behavior with the long prompt sequence.

[01:25] Dana: we also saw some hallucinations in the policy text summarization — it's small but when it happens it's bad for downstream gating.

[01:35] Priya: can you remind us what the scoring rubric is? I looked at the sheet but want to confirm thresholds for canary vs rollback.

[01:46] Ethan: sure, rubric is in the spreadsheet: intent accuracy weighted 50%, entity extraction 20%, factuality/ hallucination checks 20% (human-labeled), and latency penalty 10%. Our threshold for canary is 90 aggregate, rollback below 88. We current, again, at 87 aggregate.

[02:15] Carlos: so we're below rollback threshold, would you recommend a rollback to the previous model?

[02:23] Maya: probably yes for the canary, we should hold the rollout on production routes. We can run a targeted prompt-level A/B to see which prompts fail. Action here is to run a 10k regression on the full prompt corpus - that'll give better signal.

[02:44] Liam: timeline question: how long would the 10k regression take on Dedicated vs Hosted? We're sensitive to cost and also to noisy results from sampling.

[02:55] Ethan: on Dedicated with our current pool and batching it's about 2 hours for the 10k set with streaming disabled; on hosted it might take 3-4 hours due to throttling. Costwise, Dedicated is cheaper per-token if you commit, but obviously, there's setup.

[03:20] Priya: we also need to keep security people in the loop. Any issues with PII in the prompt set? We redacted most, but our infra team wants to make sure logs and KV cache don't persist sensitive strings.

[03:36] Maya: we can confirm that Redwood Console can mask tokens in logs, and with KMS integration we can ensure encryption at rest. We'll share the SOC2 and security FAQ.

[03:50] Carlos: good, and SSO/SAML timeline? We need SSO for our folks before we expand the test to 20 users.

[03:59] Ethan: SSO is in place for sandbox accounts, full SSO provisioning for production is scheduled for next week — I'll confirm.

[04:10] Dana: coming back to the regression, do we have automated guardrails? Like prompt templates to block certain outputs or length caps?

[04:22] Ethan: yes, Redwood has built-in guardrail policies and output filtering — we can add a safety prompt layer and enforce length caps and a hard stop token. There is also a fallback routing option to a smaller model or rule-based reply for high-risk outputs.

[04:45] Priya: what's the plan for verifying hallucination reductions? Do we have labeled examples to measure F1/precision?

[04:55] Ethan: we have a labeled set of ~350 hallucination examples; we measure factuality via human labels and report a factuality precision score. We can expand the set for the 10k run, but that requires human labeling.

[05:15] Carlos: if we do the 10k regression, can Redwood run the candidate model plus a baseline and output per-prompt diff so we can triage quickly?

[05:26] Maya: yes, we can produce a per-prompt comparison export (CSV) and attach predicted labels and scoring. We'll also flag the top 100 worst regressions.

[05:40] Liam: logging — for the regression export, can logs be anonymized and exported directly to our S3? We prefer raw token traces for debug but anonymized.

[05:52] Ethan: we can forward the export to your S3 bucket with token redaction. We'll need a short IAM role exchange.

[06:05] Priya: competitor question — has anyone tried Anthropic or OpenAI fine-tuning for these billing flows? We did a quick bench vs OpenAI and saw different hallucination patterns.

[06:17] Carlos: yeah we tested GPT-4.1 on a dev set, it did well on single-step but worse on entity extraction in mixed-format inputs.

[06:28] Maya: good signal. For next steps on the model side: run 10k regression, produce per-prompt diffs, expand hallucination labeled set, and pause production rollout until we meet threshold.

[06:45] Dana: one quick ask — can we get a recommended prompt rewrite for the billing flows? A shorter template worked better in last A/B.

[06:56] Ethan: yes, we'll include recommended prompt variants in the export and highlight ones that improved accuracy in A/B.

[07:10] Priya: timeline and owners?

[07:15] Maya: ok recap — Maya to send updated scoring spreadsheet and security docs, Ethan to schedule the 10k regression and produce per-prompt diffs, Carlos/Dana to provide any additional labeled hallucination examples, Liam to set up S3/IAM for export. We'll confirm SSO timeline.

[07:35] Carlos: sounds good, thanks everyone.

[07:38] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up w/ calendar invite for the regression kickoff and share docs by Thursday.

[07:45] End of call
